nodes.summary: For a bundled multi-stack Turing machine and every list $l$ over the alphabet of its input stack, the initial configuration of the bundled machine on $l$ equals the generic multi-stack initial configuration with $l$ on the input stack, when the main label is taken as the default label.
nodes.title: The initial configuration of a bundled multi-stack machine

nodes.summary: If the label type $\Lambda$ is finite, then every statement of a multi-stack Turing machine with labels $\Lambda$ is supported by the finite set of all labels: every label it can jump to lies in this set.
nodes.title: Every statement is supported by all labels

nodes.summary: A multi-stack Turing machine with finitely many labels is supported by the set of all its labels: this set contains the default label, and every statement of the machine is supported by it.
nodes.title: A multi-stack machine is supported by all its labels

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a multi-stack Turing machine with stacks indexed by $K$, let $k \in K$, and let $L$ be a list over the alphabet of stack $k$. The single-tape emulation of $M$, started on the tape encoding of the stacks with $L$ on stack $k$ and all other stacks empty, halts if and only if $M$, started with $L$ on stack $k$ and all other stacks empty, halts.
nodes.title: The emulation halts iff the multi-stack machine halts

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a multi-stack Turing machine whose internal state type is finite, and let $S$ be a finite set of labels that supports $M$. Then the single-tape emulation of $M$ is supported by an explicit finite set of states built from $S$ through the two translations: this set contains the initial state and is closed under the transitions of the emulation.
nodes.title: The emulation visits finitely many states

nodes.summary: For a multi-stack Turing machine $M$ with stacks indexed by $K$ and stack alphabets $\Gamma_k$, this is the single-tape machine obtained by translating $M$ first into a single-tape machine with a store and then into a plain single-tape machine. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
